name: rect_no_transform_control
_comment: The control: no element transform and no layer transform, so the evaluated bbox must equal the plain geometric bbox. Separates a runner that mis-builds the document or applies a stray matrix; it does NOT separate a port that ignores transforms (nothing to ignore), which is why the eight vectors below exist.

name: rect_translate
_comment: translate(100,50). A port that ignores the element transform returns [0,0,10,10].

name: rect_scale_nonuniform
_comment: scale(2,3) about the document origin on a rect at (5,10), so the ORIGIN moves too: [10,30,20,30]. A port that scales the size but leaves the position returns [5,10,20,30]; one that ignores the transform returns [5,10,10,10].

name: rect_rotate_45
_comment: rotate(45 degrees) about the origin of a 10x10 rect at the origin: the AABB is the square's diagonal, 10*sqrt(2) on a side, spanning x in [-5*sqrt(2), 5*sqrt(2)] and y in [0, 10*sqrt(2)]. Chosen because the answer is NOT axis-aligned-invariant: swapping b and c (the classic wrong-space slip, i.e. rotating by -45) returns [0,-7.0710678118654755,14.142135623730951,14.142135623730951] - the same extent, transposed. Ignoring the transform returns [0,0,10,10].

name: rect_skew_x
_comment: skewX with c = 0.5: x' = x + 0.5*y, so the 10x10 rect shears to a 15-wide, 10-tall AABB. Swapping b and c (skewY instead) returns [0,0,10,15] - the transpose, which is why width and height differ here.

name: rect_composed_matrix
_comment: A general matrix with every entry live (a=2 b=1 c=-0.5 d=1.5 e=7 f=-3) on a 4x6 rect at (1,2). Corners map to (8,1) (16,5) (13,14) (5,10), so the AABB is [5,1,11,13] - all four values differ from the untransformed [1,2,4,6], and swapping b and c gives [11,-2.5,14,11].

name: rect_layer_transform_only
_comment: The ANCESTOR leg: the element carries no transform and the containing layer carries translate(20,30). A port that folds only the element's own matrix returns [0,0,10,10].

name: rect_element_then_layer_order
_comment: COMPOSITION ORDER, the one thing a commuting pair cannot pin: the element scales 2x and the layer translates (5,5). Innermost-first (correct) maps (10,10) to (20,20) then to (25,25), giving [5,5,20,20]; outermost-first would give [10,10,20,20]. Same two matrices, different answer - so this vector is what separates the order.

name: rect_stroked_uses_geometric_bounds
_comment: The evaluated bbox is built from GEOMETRIC bounds, so a 4-wide stroke must NOT inflate it: [0,0,10,10], not the preview bbox [-2,-2,14,14]. The transform is the identity here so the vector isolates that one choice.

name: ellipse_no_transform_control
_comment: NON-RECT geometry starts here. The nine vectors above are all rects, where the geometric bbox IS the shape, so every one of them is blind to the family's central choice: this pass maps the four CORNERS of the geometric bbox and axis-aligns them, it does not bound the transformed shape. On a rect the two rules agree; on an ellipse or a curve they do not. Each transform-bearing vector below is paired with a control like this one -- both matrices null, so the answer must be the plain geometric bbox -- which is what lets the reference oracle take the shape's geometric bounds from the element_bounds family's own golden (named by `_geometric_bounds_from`) instead of re-deriving geometry the reference does not implement. The control is also what makes that legal: it measures, in BOTH ports, that this strokeless element's bounds() equals its geometric_bounds().

name: ellipse_rotate_45_maps_bbox_corners
_comment: THE VECTOR THE RECT-ONLY SET COULD NOT WRITE. rotate(45) on a 60x40 ellipse. Corner-mapping (the contract) gives a 70.7107-square box; bounding the ROTATED ELLIPSE gives [-25.4951,45.2156,50.9902,50.9902], a box 28 percent narrower that a viewer would see as visibly tighter around the shape. Both ports return the corner-mapped box, and so does the reference (effects._element_evaluated_bbox maps corners), so the corner rule is the ratified answer, not a shared slip -- it is what keeps the Properties panel's numbers equal to the drawn selection box (evaluated_bounds.rs module docs). This vector is what would notice a port switching to the tighter rule.

name: path_cubic_no_transform_control
_comment: Control for the curve pair: the cubic's TIGHT bbox is [0,0,20,7.5] (the hull would be 10 tall), and this vector pins that the evaluated pass starts from it.

name: path_cubic_composed_matrix
_comment: A CURVE under a general matrix (a=2 b=1 c=-0.5 d=1.5 e=7 f=-3). Corner-mapping the tight bbox [0,0,20,7.5] gives [3.25,-3,43.75,31.25]; transforming the four control points and re-bounding the resulting cubic gives [7,-3,40,23.923] -- 3.75 wider and 7.3 taller than the true curve, the error this family is DEFINED to keep, so that the panel's box matches the drawn one. Three of the four components differ, so the vector separates the rules on its own.

name: path_arc_no_transform_control
_comment: Control for the arc pair: the half elliptical arc's peak at y=-30 sets the top bound, so the geometric bbox is [0,-30,100,30].

name: path_arc_layer_rotate_90
_comment: The ANCESTOR leg on non-rect geometry: the arc carries no matrix and the LAYER rotates 90 degrees (a=0 b=1 c=-1 d=0), which transposes the box to [0,0,30,100]. A port that folded only the element's own transform returns the geometric [0,-30,100,30]; one that rotated the other way (b and c swapped) returns [-30,-100,30,100]. Three of the four components differ from the geometric bbox, and the fourth-component agreement is on x=0 only.

name: group_no_transform_control
_comment: Control for the container pair: the group's geometric bbox is the union of its two children, [5,10,100,55].

name: group_scale_2x
_comment: A CONTAINER carrying the matrix: scale(2) about the document origin, so the union's origin moves too -- [10,20,200,110], not [5,10,200,110]. Pairs with element_bounds/group_transform_is_ignored, which is the same group under a matrix in the family that must NOT fold it.
